body.statement: The randomized-treatment, monotone-employment, always-employed model of Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes embeds in the present causal class only on the following restricted submodel: \(\mathcal X\) is a singleton; the known rational assignment probabilities satisfy \(\bar\pi_z\ge\pi_*\); \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\) almost surely; \(s=+1\); both potential wages take values in the finite grid \(\mathcal Y\); and, for \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\), \(P(EE)\ge m_*>0\).  On this restricted submodel the induced law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), every unit is a complier, the always-selected-complier event equals \(EE\), and \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\).  There is no inclusion of the unrestricted Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and their sharpness conclusion does not transfer automatically outside this restriction.

attestation.note: Verified against Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes, Assumptions A--B and Proposition 1; the node records only the randomized-treatment, monotone-employment, always-employed comparison.

body.justification: This node fixes the exact restricted submodel on which the published always-employed comparison enters the present framework.
body.gap: It deliberately makes no inclusion or sharpness claim for the unrestricted published model.
body.consumer: The Job Corps proposition uses it only as a restricted comparator embedding.
